title: EMDR_Nap_Study
summary:
We are investigating whether a period of rest (afternoon nap or wakefulness) following trauma therapy is beneficial to the effectiveness of trauma therapy. To this end, we would like to compare the course of treatment of a group of patients who remain awake after therapy with another group of patients who take an afternoon nap afterwards. 
The study therefore plans for each patient to spend a regular rest period of approximately 2 hours in the sleep laboratory of the Psychiatric Institute Outpatient Clinic after each therapy session (depending on the group, approximately 90 minutes of afternoon nap or 90 minutes of wakefulness) for the duration of the therapy (12 sessions of trauma therapy with EMDR). Before and after, we want to measure how patients benefit from trauma therapy on different levels. This includes self-reports/questionnaires, clinical interviews, and a short EEG measurement that includes the response to sounds (oddball paradigm).

interventions.name: EMDR+ rest interval/ nap = (30 min preparation, including attaching electrodes for polysomnography + 90 min afternoon nap)
EMDR+ rest interval/wake = (120 min of wakefulness with undemanding activity, e.g., reading, watch movie, crossword puzzles)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of PTSD F43.1
Willingness to undergo trauma treatment with EMDR
Exclusion criteria:
- intake of medication that affects sleep (e.g., hypnotics, antidepressants, anxiolytics, beta blockers, benzodiazepines, stimulants)
- Low intelligence (IQ <80)
- Systemic, neurological, or brain disorders
- Insufficient communication skills in German
- Shift work or intercontinental flights in the last 30 days
